title: The Brilliant idea for the engine
subtitle: 科技与创新 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科技与创新（人与社会·科学与技术·科技发展与信息技术创新、科学精神）
meta: 主题语境：科技与创新（人与社会·科学与技术·科技发展与信息技术创新、科学精神）　|　核心词汇：brilliant　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 brilliant 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1973 the director wrote of ① a brilliant idea for the engine in the poster, and everybody in the theatre said at once that it was ② more brilliant than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the director, who never explained anything, had done it on the same day and gone home; it was the brilliant ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most brilliant idea for the engine anybody in the theatre had ever seen, or so the poster for August 1967 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too brilliant to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the actor who had come to help; the brilliant ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a brilliant light over the water, and said that no actor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as brilliant as the light over the water they had once had in the old theatre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was brilliant or not, and he said so.

By 1980 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the poster. What the line asked for was ⑦ something brilliant, and nothing besides. The actor from the next theatre called the whole plan ⑧ quite brilliant; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the poster kept the names of the brilliant ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1983, before dawn, she wrote of another brilliant idea for the engine in the same poster, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ more brilliant than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most brilliant light over the water in the whole theatre, she said in 1985, was the one she could never quite name; the brilliant ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 卓越（前置定语 a brilliant idea for the engine：1973 年导演在戏报里记下的那件卓越的构想）
B. adj. 卓越／明亮（比较级 more brilliant than：文中两处，一处比发动机的构想，一处比预想）
C. adj. 卓越／明亮（最高级 the most brilliant：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 卓越（表语 too brilliant to do：母亲觉得它太卓越，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 明亮（前置定语 a brilliant light over the water：叔叔把整件事称作一桩明亮的光）
F. adj. 明亮（同级比较 as brilliant as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩水面上的光相比）
G. adj. 明亮（后置定语 something brilliant：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 明亮（受程度副词修饰 quite brilliant：那位演员的评价）

items.q: a brilliant idea for the engine
the most brilliant idea for the engine anybody
a brilliant light over the water
The most brilliant light over the water in

answers.why: brilliant 意为“卓越”，1973 年导演在戏报里记下的是“一件卓越的构想”，此处作前置定语 a brilliant idea for the engine。
brilliant 意为“卓越”，此处用比较级 more brilliant than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
brilliant 意为“卓越”，戏报上 八月 那行字说它是戏院里最卓越的一件，故用最高级 the most brilliant idea for the engine。
brilliant 意为“卓越”，母亲认为这件东西“太卓越了，谁也用不上”，too brilliant to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
brilliant 意为“明亮”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩明亮的光”，此处作前置定语 a brilliant light over the water。
brilliant 意为“明亮”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩水面上的光一样明亮”，同级比较用 as brilliant as。
brilliant 意为“明亮”，戏报上那半行字要的是“明亮的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something brilliant。
brilliant 意为“明亮”，邻戏院来的那位演员认为这套计划“相当明亮”，quite 修饰原级 brilliant。
brilliant 意为“明亮”，1983 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要明亮”，故用比较级 more brilliant than。
brilliant 意为“明亮”，母亲 1985 年说的是“整个戏院里最明亮的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most brilliant light over the water。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1973 年，导演在戏报里记下了一件卓越的构想。（a brilliant idea for the engine）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更卓越。（more brilliant than …）
母亲觉得它太卓越，谁也用不上。（too brilliant to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩明亮的光。（a brilliant light over the water）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩水面上的光一样明亮。（as brilliant as …）
到了 1980 年，戏报上只剩半行字：要的是一件明亮的东西。（something brilliant）
answers: In 1973 the director wrote of a brilliant idea for the engine in the poster.
Everybody said it was more brilliant than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too brilliant to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a brilliant light over the water.
He said nobody would call it as brilliant as the light over the water they had once had.
By 1980 the poster asked for nothing but something brilliant.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 brilliant 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1973 the director wrote of a brilliant idea for the engine in the poster, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most brilliant idea for the engine in the theatre, or so the poster says.
My mother thought it too brilliant to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a brilliant light over the water, and nobody argued with him.
The actor from the next theatre called the plan quite brilliant, and everybody laughed.
The brilliant ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
